entities.name: Kashtiliash III
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Kashtiliashu III (mKaš-til-ia-šu), a Kassite monarch whose reign is tentatively placed in the mid-15th century BCE, likely governed the kingdom of Babylonia during a period of significant geopolitical flux in the ancient Near East. While his direct reign is sparsely documented, his inclusion in crucial historiographical texts like the Assyrian Synchronistic King List and the Chronicle of Early Kings attests to his legitimate, albeit perhaps brief, tenure within the long-lived Kassite dynasty, which held power over Mesopotamia for approximately 400 years following the collapse of the Old Babylonian Empire. His existence underscores the continuity of Kassite rule and their integration into the broader diplomatic and power structures of the Late Bronze Age.

The primary evidence for Kashtiliashu III stems from the monumental Assyrian Synchronistic King List (KAV 216), which records him as a contemporary of the Assyrian king Puzur-Ashur III, suggesting a co-regency or at least overlapping spheres of influence between Babylonia and Assyria around 1500 BCE. Further corroboration comes from a Kassite royal genealogy (BM 108889) that places him within the succession, though his precise relationship to other Kashtiliashu rulers remains debated by Assyriologists. The Chronicle of Early Kings also makes reference to Kassite monarchs, indirectly bolstering the historical context for his rule, which would have seen Babylonia maintaining its cultural identity and recovering from earlier periods of instability.
